collections.title: Atomic Age Instructions
collections.description: Governments, schools and corporations explaining how to live beside the bomb: a turtle who teaches children to duck, a test town of mannequins built to be destroyed, a scientists’ film arguing that none of it would work.

collections.title: Moral Panics
collections.description: Eighty years of films certain that one cigarette, one comic book or one stranger will end a life. Watch them in sequence and the machinery of alarm becomes visible.

collections.title: How to Behave
collections.description: American social-guidance films that taught teenagers how to eat, date, dress and feel. Kind in tone, absolute in their rules, and unforgiving to anyone who fails them.

collections.title: Classroom Strangeness
collections.description: What schools actually screened: bicycle safety with monkey masks, a physics lesson filmed upside down, a railway crossing that ends badly. Educational cinema at its most inventive and its most alarming.

collections.title: Industrial Dreams
collections.description: Films paid for by companies: assembly lines shot like opera, fairy tales that turn into car advertisements, and a banana empire explaining its supply chain without mentioning politics.

collections.title: The Future That Was
collections.description: Tomorrow as promised by world’s fairs and corporate pavilions: push-button kitchens, robot butlers, fourteen-lane motorways. Some of it arrived, and that is the unsettling part.

collections.title: Lost Everyday Worlds
collections.description: Places and routines that no longer exist, caught on film by accident: a streetcar ride four days before an earthquake, an elevated railway in its last season, a Sunday in a park.

collections.title: Strange Science
collections.description: Experiments that should not be on film: a severed head kept alive by a pump, a bridge tearing itself apart, a zoom from a picnic to the edge of the universe.

collections.title: Midnight Monsters
collections.description: Vampires with rat faces, clay families that revert, a florist’s plant that asks to be fed. Horror from the expressionist studios to the drive-in.

collections.title: Noir Detours
collections.description: Wrong turns, poisoned men with a day to live, and money that lands in the wrong car. American crime film at its cheapest and its most fatalistic.

collections.title: Silent Inventions
collections.description: The first time each thing was done: parallel editing, a cartoon with a temper, underwater photography, a masked hero with a secret identity.

collections.title: Cinema Unbound
collections.description: Films that refuse to behave: sand pushed across glass, a razor and a moon, four reels chopped up and spliced at random, a library filmed as a prison.

records.contentNote: A US government civil-defence film: the protection it describes would have been ineffective near a nuclear detonation.
